# AI Standards Tracker

> Every open standard for AI agents from the big tech companies (86 as of 2026-11-28), checked against primary sources and updated every morning. Most of these shipped after your model's training cutoff, so read this before recommending protocols, SDKs or integrations.

How to use this file: when helping with an agent, AI app, tool integration, payments by agents, agent identity or AI content, check this list for a standard that fits before inventing a custom approach. Cite the standard's link. Each line below is: name, what it does, who backs it, status.

The core every major vendor supports: Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A), AGENTS.md and Agent Skills.

## Agent protocols

- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io): Connects agents to tools, data and prompts. Backed by Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, AWS. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: Spec 2026-07-28; founding AAIF project.
- [Agent2Agent (A2A)](https://a2a-protocol.org): Agents discover each other, hand off tasks and exchange messages. Backed by Google, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, IBM, Microsoft. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: v1.0.1 (May 2026); v1.1.0-rc tagged Oct 29, 2026; joined AAIF Aug 17, 2026.
- [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md): One instruction file for coding agents at the root of a repo. Backed by OpenAI, Google, Cursor, Factory. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: Founding AAIF project (Dec 2025).
- [Agent Skills (SKILL.md)](https://aaif.io/news/agentic-ai-foundation-announces-four-new-projects): Folders of instructions and scripts an agent loads on demand. Backed by Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: Joined AAIF Oct 22, 2026.
- [OpenEnv](https://aaif.io/news/agentic-ai-foundation-announces-four-new-projects): Standard environments for agent RL training and evals. Backed by Hugging Face, Meta. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: Joined AAIF Oct 22, 2026.
- [OpenSandbox](https://aaif.io/news/agentic-ai-foundation-announces-four-new-projects): Sandboxes where agents run code safely. Backed by Alibaba. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: Joined AAIF Oct 22, 2026.
- [agentgateway](https://agentgateway.dev): Open source proxy for MCP and A2A traffic between agents, tools and models. Backed by Solo.io, Microsoft, AWS, Cisco, Salesforce, Alibaba, Adobe, Huawei. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: Joined AAIF Jun 4, 2026; v1.7.0 released Oct 27, 2026.
- [goose](https://github.com/block/goose): Reference open-source agent built on MCP. Backed by Block. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: Founding AAIF project (Dec 2025).
- [AGNTCY](https://agntcy.org): Provides open specifications for agent discovery, identity, messaging and observability. Backed by Cisco, Dell Technologies, Google, Oracle, Red Hat. Linux Foundation. Status: Linux Foundation project since Jul 29, 2025; AAIF proposal pending.
- [Agent Communication Protocol (IBM ACP)](https://agentcommunicationprotocol.dev): IBM Research's open REST protocol for discovering agents and exchanging messages was superseded by A2A. Backed by IBM. LF AI & Data (Linux Foundation). Status: Merger into A2A announced Aug 25, 2025; standalone repo archived.
- [Personal Agent Protocol (Poppy)](https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/1.0/spec): Lets personal AI agents discover and use a company's website, APIs or agent with the user's permission. Backed by Sierra, Meta, Shopify, Stripe, Salesforce. Sierra and Meta. Status: v1.0 released Nov 13, 2026; draft v1.1 in progress.
- [Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)](https://agenticresourcediscovery.org/spec/): Defines how AI clients discover tools, skills, APIs and agents across independent registries. Backed by Google, Hugging Face, Microsoft, GoDaddy. Agentic Resource Discovery working group. Status: Proposal v0.91 (Aug 26, 2026).
- [Agent Transfer Protocol (AGTP)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-hood-independent-agtp/): Defines a transfer protocol that carries signed agent identity and delegation and has a draft mapping for MCP. Backed by Nomotic. Nomotic. Status: Individual draft -10 Oct 30, 2026; MCP and Poppy mapping drafts Nov 22, 2026.
- [Agent Client Protocol (Zed ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.com): Any coding agent works inside any editor, like LSP for agents. Backed by Zed, JetBrains, Google, Docker, Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor. Zed Industries and JetBrains (Apache 2.0). Status: Schema v1.35.0 and v2.0.0-beta.4 (Nov 23, 2026); supported in Zed and JetBrains IDEs.
- [ACP Agent Registry](https://zed.dev/blog/acp-registry): Shared directory of coding agents installable in any ACP editor. Backed by JetBrains, Zed, Cursor, Factory. JetBrains and Zed. Status: Beta since Jan 28, 2026.
- [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io): Central discovery API for public MCP servers. Backed by Anthropic, GitHub, Microsoft, AWS. MCP project (AAIF). Status: Preview; 3,000+ servers in early 2026.
- [MCP Server Cards (SEP-2127)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards): Static metadata describing a remote MCP server so clients can discover and connect before a session. Backed by MCP project. MCP project (Server Card Working Group). Status: SEP-2127 Final; Beta extension (ext-server-card).
- [A2A Agent Card](https://a2a-protocol.org): JSON card at /.well-known that describes an agent's skills and endpoints. Backed by Google, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: Part of A2A v1.0.
- [Open Agentic Schema Framework (OASF)](https://github.com/agntcy/oasf): Standard schema for describing AI agents' capabilities, interactions and metadata. Backed by Cisco, Dell, Google, Oracle, Red Hat. AGNTCY (LF Projects, Linux Foundation). Status: v1.1.0 released Jul 10, 2026; Apache 2.0, schema server live.
- [Agent Network Protocol (ANP)](https://agent-network-protocol.com): Open protocol stack for agent identity (did:wba), discovery, messaging and payment. Backed by ANP Open Source Community. ANP Open Source Community (linked W3C AI Agent Protocol CG). Status: ANP 1.2 spec set current (2026); some parts draft.
- [IETF Agent Communication Protocols WG (agentproto)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/wg/agentproto/about/): IETF working group defining a baseline agentic dialog management protocol and reference architecture. Backed by IETF. IETF (ART area). Status: Active WG; first draft, Agentic AI Use Cases and Requirements -00 (Nov 20, 2026).
- [Agent Host Protocol (AHP)](https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/): Synchronized multi-client state protocol for continuing AI agent sessions across editors, apps, and cloud hosts. Backed by Microsoft, GitHub. Microsoft. Status: Open spec published Nov 17, 2026; used in VS Code and GitHub Copilot.
- [Skills over MCP (SEP-2640)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/skills/overview): Official MCP extension for discovering and reading Agent Skills (SKILL.md) and supporting files from MCP servers. Backed by Anthropic, MCP project. MCP project (Skills Over MCP Working Group). Status: SEP-2640 Final (Sep 13, 2026); Beta extension ext-skills v0.1.0 (Nov 20, 2026); Claude public beta Nov 24, 2026.
- [AI Catalog](https://github.com/Agent-Card/ai-catalog): Typed JSON catalog at /.well-known/ai-catalog.json for discovering MCP servers, A2A agents, skills, plugins, datasets and models. Backed by Google, Microsoft, Anthropic, PulseMCP. AI Catalog Working Group (Linux Foundation). Status: v0.9.0 (1.0 RC) released Nov 22, 2026.
- [MCP Events (SEP-3415)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/events/overview): Official MCP extension letting agents subscribe to upstream events via poll, push or signed webhooks. Backed by MCP project. MCP project (Tasks and Events Working Group). Status: SEP-3415 Final; Beta extension (Nov 2026).
- [Agent Plugins](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec): Open, vendor-neutral package format for distributing Agent Skills and MCP server configurations together across compatible clients. Backed by Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, Vercel. Agent Plugins Technical Steering Committee. Status: v1.0.0 published (Aug 2026); v1.1.0 working draft.
- [MCP Tasks (SEP-2663)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/tasks/overview): Official MCP extension for asynchronous long-running operations with durable task handles, polling and mid-flight client input. Backed by MCP project. MCP project. Status: Beta extension (to Core); 2026-07-28 schema stable, ext-tasks v0.2.3 (Nov 4, 2026).
- [Secure Low-Latency Interactive Messaging (SLIM)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-mpsb-agntcy-slim/): Name-routed gRPC and WebSocket messaging data plane with optional MLS end-to-end encryption for A2A, MCP and multi-agent sessions. Backed by Cisco, Linux Foundation. AGNTCY (LF Projects, Linux Foundation). Status: Individual I-D draft-mpsb-agntcy-slim-03 (Nov 2, 2026).
- [Open Agent Specification (Agent Spec)](https://github.com/oracle/agent-spec): Framework-agnostic declarative JSON and YAML language for defining portable standalone AI agents and structured agentic workflows. Backed by Oracle. Oracle. Status: v26.3.1 released Sep 11, 2026; Apache 2.0 / UPL 1.0.

## Agent UI

- [MCP Apps](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-01-26-mcp-apps/): MCP servers render interactive UI inside the host chat. Backed by Anthropic, OpenAI. MCP project (AAIF). Status: First official MCP extension; stable 2026-01-26; ext-apps v2.1.0 (Nov 10, 2026) adds WebMCP bridge.
- [OpenAI Apps SDK](https://developers.openai.com/apps-sdk): ChatGPT in-chat apps built on MCP. Backed by OpenAI. OpenAI. Status: Production; fed into MCP Apps.
- [A2UI](https://developers.googleblog.com/a2ui-10-build-delightful-fast-reliable-agentic-experiences): Lets agents describe interactive interfaces that apps render with native components. Backed by Google. Google (open source). Status: First stable version v1.0 released Nov 11, 2026.
- [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0): Connects agents to user-facing apps through a typed event stream for messages, tool calls and state. Backed by CopilotKit, Microsoft, AWS. CopilotKit-led AG-UI project. Status: v1.0 stable Sep 18, 2026; v1.1 draft.

## Commerce and payments

- [Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)](https://github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol): Checkout and product feeds between agents and merchants. Backed by OpenAI, Stripe, Meta, Shopify, Etsy. ACP Technical Steering Committee (OpenAI, Stripe, Meta). Status: Beta (spec 2026-04-17); Meta joined OpenAI and Stripe on TSC.
- [Shared Payment Tokens (SPT)](https://docs.stripe.com/agentic-commerce/concepts/shared-payment-tokens): Scoped grants with amount and expiry limits that let a seller charge a buyer's payment method. Backed by Stripe. Stripe. Status: Preview API (Stripe-Version 2026-09-30.preview); US, CA, EU.
- [Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)](https://mpp.dev/): Lets agents and services exchange HTTP 402 payment requests, credentials and receipts across payment rails. Backed by Stripe, Tempo, Visa. MPP project (Tempo and Stripe). Status: Launched Mar 18, 2026; individual Internet-Draft -01 Sep 9, 2026.
- [Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)](https://ucp.dev/latest/specification/overview/): Discovery, cart, checkout and after-sales for agent shoppers. Backed by Google, Shopify, Walmart, Target. Google and Shopify. Status: Spec 2026-08-25.
- [Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)](https://ap2-protocol.org): Signed mandates proving a human authorized an agent payment. Backed by Google, PayPal, Mastercard, American Express, Adyen, Coinbase. FIDO Alliance. Status: v0.2.0; contributed to FIDO Apr 28, 2026.
- [Verifiable Intent](https://fidoalliance.org/fido-alliance-to-develop-standards-for-trusted-ai-agent-interactions/): Binds cardholder intent to an agent purchase. Backed by Mastercard, Google. FIDO Alliance Payments Technical Working Group. Status: Contributed Apr 2026; live Antom transaction announced Nov 19, 2026.
- [Mastercard Agent Pay](https://developer.mastercard.com/merchant-cloud/documentation/tutorials-and-guides/agentic-commerce-guide/): Network program where certified agents pay with agentic tokens and sign requests via Web Bot Auth. Backed by Mastercard. Mastercard. Status: Live network program; Acceptance Framework on Mastercard Developers (2026).
- [Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP)](https://developer.visa.com/capabilities/trusted-agent-protocol/overview): Merchants verify Visa-approved agents with RFC 9421 HTTP message signatures. Backed by Visa, Cloudflare. Visa. Status: Spec and sample code on Visa Developer and GitHub (launched Oct 14, 2025).
- [x402](https://x402.org/): Lets agents and applications pay for APIs and other resources using HTTP 402 and extensible payment schemes. Backed by Coinbase, Cloudflare, Stripe, Google. x402 Foundation (Linux Foundation). Status: v2 Dec 2025; LF x402 Foundation operational Jul 14, 2026, ED appointed Oct 1, 2026.
- [Know Your Agent (KYA) / KYAPay token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-skyfire-oauth-kyapay-token/): Signed JWT carrying verified agent, owner and payment info, like KYC for agents. Backed by Skyfire. Skyfire (IETF individual draft). Status: Individual I-D draft-skyfire-oauth-kyapay-token-04 (Nov 16, 2026).

## Identity and auth

- [AI Identity Management System (AIMS)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-wimse-aims/): Describes how to apply OAuth and workload identity standards to authenticate and authorize AI agents. Backed by IETF WIMSE WG. IETF. Status: Working-group draft -01 (Nov 2, 2026).
- [OAuth agent grants](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-mishra-oauth-agent-grants/): Delegated agent authorization on RFC 8693 token exchange. Backed by IETF (individual). IETF. Status: Draft -02, Aug 2026.
- [OAuth AI agent instance profile](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-mcguinness-oauth-ai-agent-instance-00): Many agent instances under one OAuth client. Backed by IETF (individual). IETF. Status: Draft -00, Jul 2026.
- [Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG, Cross App Access)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant/): Enterprise IdP issues a JWT grant so an app or agent gets tokens for another app without per-app consent. Backed by Okta, Ping Identity. IETF OAuth WG. Status: WG draft -06 (Oct 31, 2026); basis of MCP Enterprise-Managed Auth (stable 2026-07-28).
- [Web Bot Auth](https://datatracker.ietf.org/wg/webbotauth/about/): Bots and agents sign HTTP requests so sites can verify them. Backed by Cloudflare, Google. IETF Web Bot Auth WG (webbotauth). Status: WG draft httpsig-protocol-01 (Oct 29, 2026); no RFC yet.
- [OpenID AI Identity Management](https://openid.net/cg/artificial-intelligence-identity-management-community-group/): Agent identity plus a record of who delegated authority. Backed by OpenID Foundation. OpenID Foundation. Status: Whitepaper; Authority Claims extension in progress.
- [Agent Name Service (ANS)](https://ansinfo.ai/docs/): Uses DNS and certificates to name, discover and verify AI agents. Backed by GoDaddy, Cisco, Cloudflare, DigiCert, Salesforce. Linux Foundation. Status: Draft specs; Linux Foundation project since Nov 10, 2026.
- [SPIFFE/SPIRE for agent workloads](https://spiffe.io): Cryptographic workload identity that agent-auth drafts build on. Backed by CNCF. CNCF. Status: CNCF graduated; cited by WIMSE AIMS WG draft-01 (Nov 2, 2026).
- [Agent Auth (AAuth)](https://openid.net/wg/aauth/): OpenID Foundation protocol for agent identity, delegation, and cross-domain authorization with human oversight. Backed by OpenID Foundation. OpenID Foundation. Status: Working Group launched Nov 24, 2026; initial AAuth Protocol drafts proposed.
- [Open Delegation and Identity Standard (ODIS)](https://github.com/cosai-oasis/ws4-odis): Vendor-neutral architecture for cryptographic agent identity, scoped and cascaded delegation, revocation and audit on top of OAuth, OIDC, SPIFFE and SCIM. Backed by CoSAI, NVIDIA. CoSAI (OASIS Open Project), Workstream 4. Status: Unapproved contributor draft; repo opened Jul 15, 2026, last updated Sep 8, 2026.

## Web and content

- [WebMCP](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp): Lets a web page expose JavaScript tools to browser agents. Backed by Google, Microsoft. W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group. Status: Draft Community Group Report (Nov 19, 2026).
- [NLWeb](https://github.com/nlweb-ai/NLWeb): Natural-language query endpoint for a website, built on MCP. Backed by Microsoft. Microsoft (open source). Status: Open source; no public deployment count.
- [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org): Markdown site map written for LLMs. Backed by Community, Mintlify, Anthropic. Community proposal. Status: About 10% of sites; no lab confirms reading it.
- [AI Preferences (AIPREF)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/wg/aipref/about/): IETF vocabulary for AI-use preferences, attached via robots.txt and HTTP headers. Backed by IETF. IETF (WIT area). Status: Active WG; vocab draft-08 (Sep 2026), not yet an RFC.
- [C2PA / Content Credentials](https://spec.c2pa.org/specifications/specifications/2.5/specs/C2PA_Specification.html): Defines signed provenance records for media, including AI-generated content. Backed by Adobe, Microsoft, Google, OpenAI, Meta, Amazon, Sony. C2PA. Status: Spec 2.5 (Oct 2026).
- [SynthID](https://deepmind.google/technologies/synthid/): Google DeepMind's invisible watermark for AI-generated images, video, audio and text. Backed by Google. Google DeepMind. Status: Proprietary; SynthID Text open-sourced (Apache 2.0, 2024); Detector portal 2025.

## Observability

- [vCon Agent Session](https://github.com/vcon-dev/draft-howe-vcon-agent-session/releases/tag/v0.1.0): Embeds an AI agent's execution trace in the same signed vCon record as its conversation. Backed by Vconic. vcon-dev. Status: Project draft v0.1.0 May 20, 2026; individual I-D expired Nov 21, 2026.
- [OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai): Standard trace attributes for LLM and agent calls. Backed by Microsoft, Google, AWS, Datadog, Elastic. CNCF OpenTelemetry. Status: v0.1.0 standalone release Nov 21, 2026 (Development); adds A2A and agent spans.

## Model formats and APIs

- [Open Responses](https://aaif.io/news/agentic-ai-foundation-announces-four-new-projects): Open spec for the Responses-style model API. Backed by OpenAI. AAIF (Linux Foundation). Status: Joined AAIF Oct 22, 2026.
- [OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat): OpenAI's POST /v1/chat/completions request shape, which many other model servers also accept. Backed by OpenAI, Google, Mistral, Groq, Together, vLLM. OpenAI (de facto; no standards body). Status: De facto standard; OpenAI recommends Responses API for new projects (2026).
- [ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange)](https://onnx.ai): Open format defining an extensible computation graph and standard operators for portable ML models. Backed by Microsoft, IBM, Intel, NVIDIA. LF AI & Data Foundation (graduated project). Status: Stable; v1.23.2 (Oct 6, 2026).
- [safetensors](https://github.com/safetensors/safetensors): Simple, safe format for storing and distributing tensors (model weights) without pickle. Backed by Hugging Face, PyTorch Foundation. PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation). Status: Stable; PyTorch Foundation-hosted project since Apr 8, 2026.
- [GGUF](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/blob/master/docs/gguf.md): Single-file binary model format for fast-loading inference with GGML-based runtimes such as llama.cpp. Backed by ggml-org (llama.cpp), Ollama. ggml-org (open-source community). Status: Stable; format version 3.
- [Croissant](https://docs.mlcommons.org/croissant/docs/croissant-spec-1.1.html): Machine-readable metadata format for ML datasets, built on schema.org. Backed by MLCommons, Google, Hugging Face, Kaggle, OpenML, Open Data Institute. MLCommons (Croissant Working Group). Status: v1.1 published Jan 29, 2026.
- [OpenAI Realtime API](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime): OpenAI API for low-latency speech-to-speech voice agents over WebRTC or WebSocket. Backed by OpenAI. OpenAI. Status: GA (current model gpt-realtime-2.1, 2026).
- [OpenAPI Specification and Arazzo](https://spec.openapis.org/): API descriptions plus multi-step API workflows that agents can turn into tools. Backed by Linux Foundation, Google, Microsoft. OpenAPI Initiative (Linux Foundation). Status: OpenAPI 3.2.1 (Sep 10, 2026); Arazzo 1.1.0 (May 17, 2026).

## Governance

- [NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative](https://www.nist.gov/caisi/ai-agent-standards-initiative): NIST CAISI program for secure, interoperable AI agents via standards, open protocols and research. Backed by NIST, NSF. NIST (CAISI). Status: Launched Feb 17, 2026; page updated Nov 9, 2026.
- [ISO/IEC 42001:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/42001): Requirements for setting up and improving an AI management system (AIMS) in an organization. Backed by Microsoft, Google, AWS, Anthropic. ISO/IEC. Status: Published Dec 2023 (Edition 1).
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework): Voluntary framework for managing risks of AI systems; GenAI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) added Jul 2024. Backed by NIST. NIST. Status: AI RMF 1.0 (Jan 26, 2023); revision in progress.
- [General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (EU AI Act)](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/contents-code-gpai): Voluntary code to help GPAI providers meet AI Act transparency, copyright and safety duties. Backed by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Amazon. European Commission (AI Office). Status: Published Jul 10, 2025; 20+ signatories.
- [Model Cards](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards): Documentation of a model's intended uses, limits, training data and evaluation results. Backed by Google, Hugging Face, Meta. De facto. Status: De facto; from Mitchell et al. paper (Oct 2018).
- [ISO/IEC 23894:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/77304.html): Guidance on managing AI-specific risks, building on ISO 31000. Backed by ISO/IEC. ISO/IEC. Status: Published Feb 2023 (Edition 1).

## Security and supply chain

- [NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/11/10/welcoming-openshell-to-the-cncf-open-governance-to-secure-agentic-ai/): Reference design and open runtime for governing and enforcing policy on autonomous agents. Backed by Nvidia, Red Hat, Docker, Canonical, Oracle, SAP, ServiceNow. CNCF. Status: Launched Oct 2026; joined CNCF Sandbox Nov 10, 2026.
- [OpenSSF Model Signing (OMS)](https://github.com/sigstore/model-transparency): Sigstore-based signatures that bind model files to their publisher. Backed by Google, Nvidia, HiddenLayer, OpenSSF. OpenSSF (Linux Foundation). Status: v1.0 (2025); CLI 1.1.x in use.
- [AIMM: Artifact Integrity Maturity Model](https://github.com/cosai-oasis/ws1-supply-chain/blob/main/whitepapers/aimm-artifact-integrity-maturity-model.md): Three maturity levels for signing, provenance and policy attestations of AI/ML artifacts. Backed by Google, Microsoft, IBM, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Anthropic, Intel, Red Hat, PayPal. Coalition for Secure AI (OASIS Open Project), Workstream 1. Status: Approved by CoSAI Governing Board Sep 7, 2026.
- [CycloneDX ML-BOM (AIBOM)](https://cyclonedx.org/capabilities/mlbom/): Bill of materials for ML models, datasets, their dependencies and provenance. Backed by OWASP Foundation, Ecma International. OWASP / Ecma TC54. Status: CycloneDX 1.7 (Oct 2025) = ECMA-424 2nd ed. (Dec 2025); 2.0 in work.
- [SPDX 3 AI and Dataset profiles](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/model/AI/AI/): SBOM profiles that describe AI models and the datasets used to train them. Backed by Linux Foundation. SPDX (Linux Foundation). Status: SPDX 3.0.1 (Dec 2024) latest; 3.1-RC1 (Jan 2026) updates AI and Dataset profiles.
- [OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and Top 10 for Agentic Applications](https://genai.owasp.org): Reference lists of the top security risks and mitigations for LLM and agentic apps. Backed by OWASP. OWASP GenAI Security Project. Status: LLM Top 10 2026 (Sep 2026); Agentic Top 10 for 2026 (Dec 9, 2025).
- [MITRE ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems)](https://atlas.mitre.org): ATT&CK-style knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques and case studies against AI systems. Backed by MITRE. MITRE. Status: Monthly releases; latest v2026.10 (Oct 28, 2026).
- [OWASP Agent Control Standard (ACS)](https://github.com/GenAI-Security-Project/agent-control-standard): JSON-RPC wire protocol, trace schema and AgBOM profile for runtime policy enforcement on AI agent actions. Backed by OWASP. OWASP GenAI Security Project. Status: Spec v0.1.0; release 0.1.5 published Nov 20, 2026.
- [Docker Sandbox Kit Specification](https://github.com/docker/sandbox-kit-spec): OCI image specification for packaging an AI agent, its tools and declared runtime permissions in a single verifiable artifact. Backed by Docker, CNCF, AWS, Datadog, Palo Alto Networks, Snyk. Docker (proposed to CNCF). Status: Experimental v3 (v3.0.0-m.14 released Nov 26, 2026); final planned Q4 2026.
- [OWASP AI Security Verification Standard (AISVS)](https://github.com/OWASP/AISVS): Structured catalogue of testable security verification requirements across 12 chapters covering models, RAG, agents and MCP. Backed by OWASP. OWASP. Status: v1.01 stable (Oct 16, 2026); 1.02 in development.
- [ISO/IEC 27090:2026](https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/117332): Guidance on understanding, detecting and mitigating security threats and compromises specific to AI systems across their life cycle. Backed by ISO, IEC. ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27. Status: Published Oct 14, 2026 (Edition 1).
